title: Multi-frequency observations of PDS70c: Radio emission mechanisms in the circumplanetary environment
question: What is the radio emission mechanism of the circumplanetary environment around PDS 70c, and why is PDS 70c detected in the sub-millimetre continuum while PDS 70b is not?

data.sensitivity: Band 3: 4.68 uJy/beam; Band 4: 4.06 uJy/beam; Band 7: 14 uJy/beam (single EBs ~20–30 uJy/beam in natural weights); Band 9: 115 uJy/beam

what.value: Archival ALMA Band 3 datasets from projects 2022.1.00893.S and 2022.1.01477.S

evidence.quote: We also include in our analysis the archival datasets for Bands 3, from ALMA projects 2022.1.00893.S (cite: Doi2024ApJ...974L..25D) and 2022.1.01477.S (cite: Liu2024ApJ...972..163L).

what.value: 2017 and 2019 Band 7 flux densities and positions of PDS 70c

evidence.quote: The same imaging strategy as for the 2017 and 2019 Band 7 datasets (cite: CasassusCarcamo2022MNRAS.513.5790C; Casassus2023MNRAS.526.1545C) was extended to the other bands.

what.value: Coordinates of protoplanets PDS 70b and PDS 70d

evidence.quote: The two circles in each of the images in Fig. 1 are centred on the positions of b and d, using the co-ordinates provided by (cite: Wang2021AJ....161..148W) and (cite: Christiaens2024A&A...685L...1C).

what.value: Solar photospheric abundances and collisional ionisation potentials of H, He, Na, Mg, and K

evidence.quote: For this we used the abundances and collisional ionisation potentials of the most relevant elements in the solar photosphere, shown in Table 1 (cite: Asplund2009ARA&A..47..481A; Lide2008chcp.book.....L; Sarah2014MNRAS.440...89K).

what.value: Planetary mass constraints and orbital radius of PDS 70c

evidence.quote: We opted for a planetary mass of $M_{\rm p}=4 \, M_{\rm Jup}$, given the upper limit of $4.9 \, M_{\rm Jup}$ (cite: Doi2024ApJ...974L..25D) and the restriction of $4 \, M_{\rm Jup}<M_{\rm p}< 12 \, M_{\rm Jup}$ (cite: Haffert2019NatAs...3..749H).
and we adopted a planetary orbital radius for PDS 70c of $34 \, {\rm au}$ (cite: Haffert2019NatAs...3..749H)

recipe.goal: Self-calibrate, align, and image multi-frequency ALMA visibility data
recipe.method: Perform automatic user-independent phase and amplitude self-calibration with snow (using gpuvmem and CASA gaincal/applycal), align visibility datasets in position and flux scale using VisAlign, concatenate array configurations (except Band 7 TM2, and uv-clipping Band 9 TM1 < 0.4 Mlambda), and restore continuum images.
key_parameters: Briggs robustness parameter r = 2 during self-calibration; final images restored with r = 1.0 (Band 3), r = 1.0 (Band 4), r = 0.0 (Band 7), r = 2.0 (Band 9)
Band 9 TM1 uvrange clipped to discard baselines shorter than 0.4 Mlambda; TM1 intensity scaled by 1/0.78 and TM2 shifted by dRA = 25.6 mas, dDec = 0.13 mas
assumptions: Point source at Band 3 phase centre coincides with GAIA ICRS position of PDS 70 and is due to accretion free-free emission on the central star

recipe.goal: Extract multi-frequency photometry and spectral indices of PDS 70c and central star
recipe.method: Search for counterparts at expected orbital positions of PDS 70 b, c, d; measure PDS 70c flux density via peak intensity in restored images, elliptical Gaussian fits in deconvolved images, and forced photometry for non-detections (Bands 3 and 9); compute two-frequency and multi-frequency power-law spectral indices.
key_parameters: Band 9 forced photometry aperture radius = 3 times rms pointing accuracy (~5 mas); reference frequency nu_0 = 145 GHz for power-law spectral index fit
assumptions: Circular orbit around a 0.97 M_sun star in the plane of the disc with PA = 160 deg and inclination i = 130 deg; positional uncertainty taken as 1/10 clean beam major axis in natural weights

recipe.goal: Assess Band 7 variability of PDS 70c across 2023 epochs
recipe.method: Align all 9 execution blocks (7 epochs) to 23 May 2023 with VisAlign after amplitude+phase self-calibration; subtract PDS 70c from the gpuvmem disc model via elliptical Gaussian fit, simulate disc visibilities with pyralysis and subtract from observations; fit a point source in the uv plane at fixed centroid position for each spectral window and epoch.
key_parameters: Reference epoch: 23 May 2023; channels collapsed in each of the 4 spectral windows

recipe.goal: Fit parametric CPD SED models (dusty disc, jet, H I free-free, uniform slab, and magnetic disc with metals and H-)
recipe.method: Construct analytic and semi-analytic SED models for a dusty viscous CPD, a dusty CPD plus optically thin/thick ionised jet, a viscous CPD with H I free-free emission, a uniform pill-box slab, and a magnetised CPD with metal and H- free-free and bound-free opacities; sample posterior parameter distributions against the coeval Bands 3, 4, 7, and 9 SED using Nautilus.
key_parameters: M_p = 4 M_Jup, d = 112.3 pc, orbital radius = 34 au, R_out = 1/3 R_Hill ~ 1.23 au, R_p = R_in = 1 R_Jup, kappa_R = 10 cm^2/g, T_floor = 27 K, mu = 1
Jet spectral index alpha_jet = 0.4 (optically thick) or -0.1 (optically thin); magnetic disc alpha(R) > 10^-5
assumptions: Dust opacity kappa_mm = 3.4 * zeta * (0.87 mm / lambda) cm^2/g; hydrostatic Gaussian vertical gas profile; LTE ionisation via Saha equation; solar photospheric abundances for H, He, Na, Mg, K without dust depletion; n_i = n_H- = n_e = 0 when H- >= 10% of ions

recipe.goal: Simulate CPD surface shock emission and test photospheric shock vs CPD surface shock scenarios
recipe.method: Fit uniform slab model with fixed R_max = 2 R_Jup to test photospheric shock/accretion funnels; perform two 1D post-shock gas simulations following Aoyama et al. (2018) to compute optical depth and temperature profiles at 300 GHz and 600 GHz; derive mass influx rates and upper limits on planetary accretion rate.
key_parameters: Pre-shock velocities and densities: (v_0, n_0) = (30 km/s, 10^15 cm^-3) and (50 km/s, 10^12 cm^-3); mean molecular weight mu = 1.35; effective slab radius R_max = 62 R_Jup at 7000 K
assumptions: Pre-shock velocity equals free-fall velocity v_0 = sqrt(2 G M_p / r); spatially constant mass flux falling on both sides of a circular slab

answer_key.quantity: Dust-to-gas ratio upper limit in CPD (fixed alpha = 10^-2 model)

evidence.quote: The inferred upper limits on the dust-to-gas ratio are $10^{-4.80}$ and $10^{-7.05}$ for the models with fixed $\alpha$ and fixed $\dot{M}_{\rm p}$, respectively.
Given an optically thick free-free spectrum, any steeper component is negligible, and the dust-to-gas mass ratio $\zeta$ must be very low, $\log(\zeta)<-4.80$.

answer_key.quantity: Planetary accretion rate upper limit log(Mdot_p / (M_Jup yr^-1)) for B_ps = 610 G

evidence.quote: Using the magnetic disc model from Sec. 3.5 with the best fit value of $B_{\rm ps}=610$ G, we obtain an upper limit of $\log \left(\dot{M}_{\rm p}/(M_{\rm Jup}/\rm yr)\right)<-5.42$ using the 3 $\sigma$ flux limit in Band 7.

score_reason: ALMA project codes, observing logs, self-calibration logic, visibility alignment shifts/scalings, extracted flux densities, and analytic model equations are thoroughly documented, but the custom non-parametric deconvolution/alignment stack (snow, gpuvmem, VisAlign, pyralysis) lacks exact regularisation/grid parameters and the custom SED/shock modelling scripts are not released.
rediscovery_reason: The raw ALMA datasets are publicly identifiable by project code in the ALMA archive, the multi-frequency flux densities and spectral indices of PDS 70c are quantitative, and the analytic CPD and uniform-slab equations are written out in full.
